summary: 15-min product demo focused on Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and invoice reconciliation features. Customer is concerned about attributing spend across teams and matching Redwood bill to internal invoices. Discussed pilot with Dedicated capacity for predictable bursts; agreed to run targeted benchmarks and exchange anonymized traffic samples.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-04-28
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Sean Park (Redwood AE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Alex Morales (Tempestia CTO), Priya Nair (Director of Platform), Carlos Vega (SRE), Lina Soto (Finance)

Summary: Quick demo of Console focusing on how Tempestia can map per-route usage back to internal team chargebacks and reconcile Redwood invoices to their billing system. Conversation includes pilot plan and data exchange steps.

00:00 Alex Morales: alright everyone, thanks for doing this, i know schedules are tight so i'll hand it to Sean to kick off
00:06 Sean Park: awesome thanks Alex, hey team, real quick agenda — show you the Console route insights, how billing breaks down per route and per-team, then the invoice reconciliation export, and we can talk pilot options, sound good?
00:18 Priya Nair: sounds good, our main goal is to be able to say which product teams are driving cost, and then match that to our monthly invoices so finance isn't angry, right Lina?
00:28 Lina Soto: yes please, that and being able to explain spikes when they happen, we had a weird $12k blip last month we still don't understand
00:36 Maya Liu: got it, we'll show the per-route heatmaps and the export that maps tokens to routes, and also a suggested mapping to your internal teams using tags or route labels
00:50 Carlos Vega: quick question on sample retention — how long does Redwood keep per-request traces? we already have retention limits so we can't store PII longer than 30 days
01:02 Sean Park: good question, by default hosted retains 30 days for request metadata; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention via config and we support redaction and KMS for payload encryption, we can also do shorter retention windows
01:22 Alex Morales: ok before demo — are you proposing we do a Dedicated pilot? we liked the predictability but worried about cost relative to hosted bursty patterns
01:33 Maya Liu: yeah that's a common tradeoff — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better tail latency; Console Optimize can suggest batching and quantization profiles to reduce token cost for your workload, we usually run a short benchmark to estimate unit cost
01:48 Priya Nair: can you show how the Console ties requests to a route and then to a team? we tag requests at the edge today but mapping is messy
01:58 Maya Liu: sure — navigating to Console > Usage > Routes. here's the route list, you can see columns like requests, avg latency, token count, model variant, and cost-per-token estimate
02:24 Maya Liu: (screen) ok this route is /api/generate/chat-product — if you click it you get time-series of requests and a breakdown by token types, and we also show cost attribution by attribution_key which for many customers is a header like x-team-id or a route label
02:45 Priya Nair: the x-team-id header is available, but sometimes clients call via gateways that strip custom headers, is there a fallback?
02:54 Maya Liu: yes you can map IPs, auth-subjects from JWTs, or use prefix-based routing. we also support automatic inference heuristics, they aren't perfect but they help bulk-map unknowns
03:12 Carlos Vega: and for invoice reconciliation — can we export line items with route-level granularity? our AR team needs a CSV that matches our chargeback model
03:21 Sean Park: yep — go to Billing > Exports. we have an invoice line export that includes date, route, attributed_team, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, unit_cost, and a billable_amount column. can generate CSV, Parquet for BigQuery, or send to an S3 bucket
03:40 Lina Soto: Parquet to BigQuery would be ideal for us, we run joins against internal billing tables
03:46 Sean Park: perfect — we can set an S3 export to push daily files in Parquet. for reconciliation we also include a checksum/manifest so you can validate file integrity
03:58 Alex Morales: small nit — sometimes models spin up different variants during fallbacks, do you preserve which variant served each token?
04:08 Maya Liu: yes, each token event includes model_variant and fallback_reason if a fallback occurred. note transcription: sometimes our export field named "model_variant" gets transcribed as 'mold varient' in notes, but it's model_variant in the API
04:26 Priya Nair: ok show me a real example of a spike and how you'd trace it to a team and then to a particular route.
04:33 Maya Liu: sure — switching to the last 30 days, selecting the spike window... here you can overlay route-level traces and drill into a single request timeline. see this request — we show prefix cache hits (we call it KV cache in the product but the transcript might say K V cash), token counts per step, and the client headers that led us to attribute it to team-42
05:05 Carlos Vega: hmm the cache hit info is helpful — can we export those request timelines for a forensic review?
05:12 Maya Liu: yes, there's an 'Export Request Trace' button, it redacts PII by default but you can choose a full trace for SREs with an elevated role, we support RBAC so only certain users can see raw payloads
05:24 Alex Morales: security-wise we need SOC2 plus SAML SSO and our KMS for key management, does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
05:33 Sean Park: yes on Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK options and we have SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 — we'll send the compliance pack
05:46 Priya Nair: ok great. about cost — can Console show us modeled cost if we apply different batching or quantization profiles? we want to know trade-offs before we commit to Dedicated
05:56 Maya Liu: yep that's where Optimize suggestions come in — Console Optimize runs simulation on sampled traffic and returns estimated cost-per-route under different settings e.g., 8-bit quantization or batching window of 50ms. i'll show an example run we did for another customer
06:15 Maya Liu: (screen) here are three scenarios: "Baseline (hosted)" "Optimized (quant 8-bit)" and "Dedicated w/ packing". each shows projected token cost and projected SLO impact. the simulation uses your traffic sample if you provide it, otherwise a heuristic model
06:36 Alex Morales: can we see the assumptions for the sim? like tokenization differences across request types?
06:41 Maya Liu: yes the output includes assumptions: sample size, percentile latency target, avg seq len, and model perf bench used. we try to be transparent — the sim is a guidance not a guarantee
06:53 Carlos Vega: about the pilot — our ops prefer something that can emulate bursts on demand. can Redwood Dedicated scale quickly or is it reserved capacity only?
07:03 Sean Park: Dedicated is reserved pools with configurable autoscale policies; you can request burst capacity for short windows. for unpredictable workloads we often recommend a hybrid: Hosted for large unpredictable spikes + Dedicated baseline for steady traffic
07:20 Priya Nair: what's the billing model for a hybrid? is the billable unit separated cleanly?
07:26 Sean Park: yes we report usage and reserved capacity costs separately. Console > Billing shows both line items and a blended unit cost if you want that, and exports separate columns for reserved_hours and burst_hours
07:37 Lina Soto: ok can you show how a single invoice looks when we have hybrid usage?
07:42 Sean Park: sure switching to demo invoice... (screen) here's an invoice with sections: reserved capacity, on-demand usage, data transfer, and rate card metadata. we include mapping to your internal charge codes if you provide them during onboarding
08:00 Alex Morales: great. question from compliance: will we get access logs for every Console user action? auditors want immutable logs
08:09 Jordan Kim: yes, audit logs are available and we can export them to your SIEM or S3 with immutability flags; we also support log TTLs per your retention policy
08:21 Priya Nair: ok back to reconciliation — show a fail-case where a route switched model variants mid-run and how we'd account for that on the invoice
08:30 Maya Liu: mm-hmm — here's an example. route /api/embeds switched from open-llama-v1 to open-llama-quant at t=03:12 due to capacity. the request-by-request export shows model_variant per request so finance can reconcile which tokens incurred which rates
08:50 Lina Soto: if that happens will we see a sudden change in unit cost? and can Console flag anomalies automatically?
08:58 Maya Liu: yes the anomaly detector flags big jumps in unit_cost-per-route and can send alerts to Slack or PagerDuty. it also creates a suggested investigation note with the top correlated signals
09:16 Carlos Vega: speaking of alerts, what about SLO tracking integrated with routes? we want per-route error budgets and notify when close to breach
09:25 Maya Liu: Console supports per-route SLOs, you can set a target and it tracks burn rate; it can enforce fallback policies too, like revert to a cheaper variant if error rate crosses threshold
09:40 Alex Morales: can you simulate an invoice reconciliation for our last billing period using our data?
09:45 Sean Park: yes that's part of the pilot scope — we can run a dry reconciliation and produce a reconciliation report that maps Redwood line items to your internal ledger. need your traces and mapping table.
09:58 Priya Nair: i'll put together the mapping table, but to be clear we need anonymized traces. what format do you prefer?
10:06 Maya Liu: Parquet with columns: timestamp, route, attributed_key, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, fallback_reason; redaction can remove payloads. Priya: you ok with Parquet?
10:14 Priya Nair: yes Parquet works. we'll try to get it by 2026-04-30.
10:20 Sean Park: perfect. quick note on pricing structure for the pilot — we can offer a one-month reduced reserved capacity rate if you agree to a 3-month evaluation, otherwise pay-as-you-go on Hosted. I'll send details
10:34 Alex Morales: who else from Redwood will we be working with during the pilot?
10:37 Sean Park: Maya will run benchmarks and performance tuning, Jordan handles onboarding and compliance artifacts, and I'll be your commercial contact
10:46 Jordan Kim: and my team will set up the S3 export and SOC2 package access, i'll send the onboarding checklist after this call
10:53 Lina Soto: good. smaller question — can we filter billing exports by project code? we tag things in our internal system by project
11:01 Maya Liu: yes you can add arbitrary metadata on routes (project, product-line) and then use that in the exports and dashboard filters. we'll also show aggregation hierarchies so you can roll-up teams to orgs
11:16 Carlos Vega: quick technical — for the benchmark, what environment do you run on? we prefer cloud region eu-west-1
11:22 Maya Liu: we can run on eu-west-1; our Dedicated test harness can provision the same GPU instance types you use in production for apples-to-apples numbers
11:34 Priya Nair: any chance you can include a model with 4-bit quant in the sim? we want to see aggressive compression numbers
11:40 Maya Liu: yes we support 4-bit sims but we flag potential quality regressions. Optimize will show expected change in perplexity or a simple quality delta on your eval set if you provide one
11:52 Alex Morales: ok looks good. final recap?
11:56 Sean Park: recap: Tempestia to supply anonymized Parquet trace and mapping table by 2026-04-30, Redwood to provide pricing sheet and pilot contract by 2026-05-02, Maya to run benchmark week of 2026-05-06 and produce an Optimize sim, Jordan to send onboarding checklist and SOC2 pack.
12:18 Priya Nair: yep that's perfect. thanks everyone.
12:22 Alex Morales: thanks y'all. will look out for the docs
12:26 Sean Park: thanks, we'll follow up in email and put the next meeting on calendar after the sample is in. bye.
12:34 END OF TRANSCRIPT

Notes on transcription: speaker overlap occasional; some product terms transcribed oddly (e.g., "KV cache" -> "K V cash") and model variant spelled "mold varient" in one auto-caption, corrected above where necessary.
